acquisition_task: Blinded acquisition of Liber Linteus Zagrabiensis Column XI (phase 1: acquire D0 diplomatic text from an independent source).

blinding_attestation.allowed_knowledge: P-1 through P-5 designate Column XI as a prospective holdout (from task description only).
blinding_attestation.statement: The prediction manifest (agents/jethro/reports/data/liber-linteus/prediction_manifest.json) was not opened. No exact P-1..P-5 prediction texts or scoring criteria were read from any location. Incidental public-source exposures to isolated Column XI lexical items (from web search snippets and Wikipedia) are recorded separately in xi_contamination_ledger.json; these were not sought and do not constitute acquisition of Column XI text.

d0_d1_omitted_reason: No source meeting the sufficient-fidelity bar was acquired. Per protocol, D0/D1 files are not created on SOURCE_GAP: writing empty files would misrepresent the outcome, and writing inferred or low-fidelity text would violate the holdout. No Column XI tokens were transcribed.
fidelity_bar: Diplomatic (D0) transcription must come from an independently accessible facsimile or scholarly transcription containing Column XI, with line-level addressability sufficient to assign LL.XI:{LINE} addresses. A low-reliability amateur transcription with admitted poor source images and unreadable letters (Copeland/Maravot) does not meet this bar and was not used.
outcome_detail: No independently accessible facsimile or scholarly transcription containing Column XI at sufficient diplomatic fidelity was found. The modern scholarly Column XI text (Rix, Etruskische Texte II; van der Meer 2007; Belfiore 2010) exists only in print editions with no accessible online copy located. The 1892 Krall editio princeps is accessible in principle via Internet Archive and HathiTrust scans, but: (a) the IA full-text fetch timed out and was not retryable per instruction; (b) HathiTrust denied access (HTTP 403); (c) a second Krall scan (Reinach/MOM PDF) timed out and was not retryable per instruction; (d) pass-1's OCR of the IA Krall scan lacked Column XI entirely, so even a successful Krall fetch would not have been known to contain XI. No reconstruction, inference, substitution of another column, or prediction scoring was performed.
